01 / Product overview · for a first broker conversation

Rhythm Bound
CRM for commercial insurance brokers

Rhythm Bound will bring client information, insurance work and relationship history into one place. It will read the email and documents you already receive, prepare the next steps, and show you what needs a decision.

01

Client intelligence

See the business, its people, assets, policies and service history together. Check a fact against the email or document it came from.

02

Opportunity orchestration

Move new business, renewals and coverage changes through missing information, submissions, carrier questions, quotes and binding.

03

Relationship dynamics

See who knows the people who decide, what has changed in the relationship, and who should make the next contact.

Product walkthrough · 26 October 2026 · Proposed screens and fictional examples
02 / How the parts connect

One email can update all three parts.

The client uses ordinary email. Rhythm Bound prepares the work behind it; the broker stays in control of what happens next.

Example · Lakeshore Paving → broker
“We bought another paver, invoice attached. Can you send a certificate for the city job by Friday?”
Fictional client and request, used throughout this guide.
↓

Intake reads the email and invoice

Matches the client, extracts the equipment details, recognises the request and links the sources.

↓

Client intelligence

Adds the paver to the equipment register for confirmation. Keeps the invoice beside the extracted values.

Opportunity orchestration

Starts the coverage-change work and prepares a certificate draft. Tracks Friday’s deadline and the cover still to confirm.

Relationship dynamics

Records that the client initiated contact and asked before acting. This adds context to the relationship history.

↓

Today · Broker’s decision

Check the paver details, review the change request, and establish the cover before issuing a certificate that relies on it.

An equipment entry is a fact about the client. A change request is work in progress. Coverage is effective only when the required authority and supporting evidence establish it.

03 / Today

Start with the few things that need you.

Each item says what happened, why it matters and what is ready to do. Open the evidence, change the draft, approve it, or defer it.

Work already prepared

Draft client questions, carrier replies and next steps come from the record. You add the judgement.

Follow-up with a reason

A deadline, an unanswered question or a renewal prompts attention. Timing is set for the brokerage.

One place to return to

Open the client or placement workspace for detail, then return to the decisions that remain.

04 / Client intelligence

Know the client without rebuilding the file.

Business details, ownership, people, locations, equipment, policies and correspondence form one connected client record.

Read what already exists

Emails, policies, schedules, spreadsheets, invoices and photos supply the starting facts. Confirm new clients and uncertain matches.

Correct once

A correction updates current views and future drafts. Original evidence and versions already sent remain in the history.

Keep uncertainty visible

Extracted, client-stated, inferred, broker-assessed, confirmed, conflicting and missing values remain distinguishable.

“Equipment cover not in our record” means the record needs checking. It does not establish that the client has no equipment insurance.

05 / Relationship dynamics

Know the right people. Know when to act.

A client can have strong day-to-day contact and still have a gap with the person who approves the premium. Look across the whole brokerage to see who already knows whom.

People and roles first

A “field of play” is one part of a client’s business, such as commercial insurance, with its own decision-makers and influencers.

Explain the reading

Contact history, who initiated it, meetings and changes in tone support the view. Thin history is shown as insufficient history.

Make a sensible next move

Use an existing relationship for an introduction. Leave a quiet, healthy relationship alone. More activity is not the goal.

Mailbox reading is opt-in. Calls are logged by the broker in a couple of taps. Sentiment is the system’s reading of client-written text, shown with its source sentence; it is not an employee performance measure.

06 / Opportunity orchestration

Carry the information through to placement.

Prepare the submission from the client record, keep each carrier’s questions distinct, compare the offers, and record what was approved and bound.

Find the gaps

Use what is known; ask only for missing or changed information.

Prepare the forms

Reuse answers in the CSIO application and carrier supplements.

Coordinate questions

Share an answer when subject, period and scope match.

Compare quotes

Show price, terms, exclusions and source wording together.

Record the placement

Keep client instructions, authority, effective terms and evidence.

Answer once, use it where it fits

The question bank maps the same fact to the forms that need it. A five-year claims question and a three-year claims question still get their own period-correct answers.

Keep service and renewals moving

Changes, certificates and renewal work use the same record. The default renewal contact asks “what’s changed?” rather than asking the client to start again.

07 / Using it in your brokerage

Start with the way you work today.

The first conversation should test this against a real client file: where the information arrives, what gets retyped, what stalls, and which people need to be involved.

01 / Bring the book across

Import the existing policy list

Map clients, contacts, carriers, policy numbers, premiums and renewal dates from a spreadsheet. Review uncertain matches.

02 / Connect the work

Choose mailboxes and carriers

Review a digest of the last six months of connected mail. Set submission routes, forms, permissions and follow-up timing.

03 / Agree the fit

Walk through one live workflow

Identify the system that owns current policy data if an existing broker system stays. Agree how changes are reconciled.

What you would keep doing

Confirm new clients, check uncertain facts, log what only you know, and approve substantive messages and transaction instructions.

What we would test together

Accuracy on your documents, time spent retyping, repeated client questions, delays through placement, and whether suggested follow-ups help.

For the conversation: Show us a recent renewal or new-business file from first email to final placement. Where did your team have to enter the same information again? Where did the work wait? Who held the missing context?
Basis of this walkthrough and product scope

Prepared from Rhythm Bound PRD Draft 1.0, 26 October 2026 (PRD_10.md), especially PART.1–7, E01–E08, E13, E19–E23, RELP and SCORE; and the Painkiller Labs Company Overview and Narrative Guide, October 2026.

The Painkiller Labs foundation describes five capabilities. This guide uses the three product parts named in the Rhythm Bound PRD. Market signals inform the broader company approach; the PRD’s learning loop uses carrier questions, wins, declines and follow-up outcomes. Client feedback is a reserved placeholder in this PRD. Direct and simulated feedback are therefore not shown as specified Rhythm Bound features.

Every screen here is a proposed illustration rendered for this document, not a screenshot of a released product. Client names, messages, asset values, carriers and quote terms are fictional. This walkthrough describes intended behaviour; it does not set a delivery date or change the application.
